content.text: The "Add Task" button in the checklist template editor is fundamentally broken — clicking it (via both real and programmatic click, on a fresh page load, with no JS errors) never adds an item row, and the form saves templates with 0 tasks with no validation. I confirmed this at the DB level: `checklist_templates.items` is an empty jsonb array. This is a new, reproducible defect blocking criterion 4. I'll seed template items via SQL to scope the downstream impact (whether the job-checklist flow would work if items existed), then move to testing the other three areas.

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request — the
  controller's only touchpoint into this context, so it never sees
  event data it can't trust.
  """
  def receive_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :paid, :succeeded)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :unpaid, :failed)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:ok, :ignored}

  defp find_invoice_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => invoice_id}} when is_binary(invoice_id) ->
        fetch_invoice(invoice_id)

      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) ->
        fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id)

      _ ->
        {:error, :invoice_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice(invoice_id) do
    case Repo.get(Invoice, invoice_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Invoice, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

input.title: Checklist template editor: "Add Task" button never adds an item row; templates save with 0 tasks
input.description:
On /quality/templates/new (and presumably /quality/templates/:id/edit), clicking "Add Task" (button[data-test="add-template-item-button"], phx-click dispatches a "change" event to #new-form) does not add any new checklist item input row to the form. Verified on a fresh page load with no prior interaction, using both a real browser click and a programmatic element.click() — no JS errors were thrown (window.onerror trap empty), and the LiveView socket was connected. The <div data-test="template-items"> container still only contains the empty <!-- inputs_for --> comment placeholder and the hidden items_drop input after clicking the button 1-3 times.

Consequence: "Save Template" happily saves a template with 0 items (checklist_templates.items = {} in the DB) with no client or server validation preventing this, so there is no way to create a checklist template with real tasks through the UI at all.

I confirmed the downstream flow is otherwise correct: after manually seeding checklist_templates.items via SQL with 3 sample tasks, the job's field checklist at /field/jobs/:id correctly rendered the template's exact tasks (grouped by room), checking them off and completing the job correctly produced a "Proof of Work" section on the invoice listing the completed tasks. So the defect is isolated to the item-add interaction in template_form_component.ex (likely the JS.dispatch("change") pattern for the inputs_for "add" button not carrying the button's name/value into the dispatched change event, or a mismatched form target).

Reproduction: log in as owner, go to /quality/templates/new, fill Name, optionally select a Property, click "Add Task" — nothing happens. Click "Save Template" — template saves with Tasks: 0 shown in the list.

Blocks story 836 criterion "Invoice shows the job's proof-of-work" end-to-end via the UI (had to seed items via SQL to verify the rest of the flow).
